description: Expected APRE results for the seeded sandbox scenarios. Names are IAM names (prefix 'apre-'). This file is the answer key used to measure detection (true positives) and false alarms (decoys) in Phase II evaluation.

expected_paths.title: Role chain from intern to sensitive S3 data

hops.via: sts:AssumeRole (permission granted through group apre-interns; role trusts intern)

expected_paths.title: Support user can rewrite own policy to become admin
expected_paths.technique: iam:CreatePolicyVersion on a policy attached to self
expected_paths.reference: Rhino Security Labs IAM privesc method 1; pathfinding.cloud IAM-001

expected_paths.title: Deployer can run code as an admin role through Lambda
expected_paths.reference: Rhino Security Labs IAM privesc method 15

hops.via: iam:PassRole to a role trusting lambda.amazonaws.com, plus permission to create and invoke functions

decoys.why_not_exploitable: Has iam:PassRole but no lambda:CreateFunction / InvokeFunction or any other service that could use the role.

decoys.looks_like: S1 (assume data role, read sensitive bucket)
decoys.why_not_exploitable: Identity policy allows sts:AssumeRole on apre-data-role, but the role's trust policy does not trust the contractor. Both sides are required.
The editable policy (apre-unattached-policy) is attached to no principal, so editing it grants nothing.

scoring_inputs_note: Impact and likelihood values are assigned by the risk-scoring engine, not here. This file records only what exists and whether it is exploitable.
